lit: to spread things out lavishly and waste them

use.how: Predicate or object of 反对/避免: 婚礼不要铺张浪费。 Criticises showy, excessive spending of money or materials, often on events or public funds.

near.diff: 挥金如土 describes a person throwing money around like dirt; 铺张浪费 criticises the lavish scale and waste of an event, a lifestyle or public spending.

cue: A company holds a year-end banquet with far more dishes than anyone can eat and fireworks no one asked for. How would a critic describe it?

ctx.s: 婚礼简单一点就好，没必要{铺张浪费}。
ctx.en: A simple wedding is fine; there's no need to be extravagant.

ctx.s: 点了一桌子菜，最后剩了一大半，真是{铺张浪费}。
ctx.en: We ordered a whole table of dishes and left more than half; what a waste.

ctx.s: “年会要搞得这么大吗？这不是{铺张浪费}吗？”
ctx.en: "Does the annual party have to be this big? Isn't that just wasteful extravagance?"

ctx.s: 他虽然很有钱，生活却一点也不{铺张浪费}。
ctx.en: Although he is very rich, he lives without any extravagance at all.

ctx.s: 政府部门应当带头反对{铺张浪费}，节约每一分公款。
ctx.en: Government departments should lead the way in opposing extravagance and save every cent of public money.

ctx.s: 这场开幕式花了大量经费，被不少网友批评{铺张浪费}。
ctx.en: The opening ceremony cost a huge sum and many people online criticised it as extravagant and wasteful.

bad.s: 我的手机坏了，只好{铺张浪费}买了一个新的。
bad.en: (meant: my phone broke, so I had to spend money on a new one)
bad.why: Replacing something you need is not extravagance; the idiom criticises showy, excessive spending.

bad.s: 他上课总是{铺张浪费}时间。
bad.en: (meant: he always wastes time in class)
bad.why: The idiom takes no object and is about lavish spending of money or things; for time, use the plain verb làngfèi with its object.

lit: what comes in does not cover what goes out

use.how: Predicate about the finances of a person, household or organisation: 公司已经入不敷出。 Describes a situation, not a character.

near.diff: 捉襟见肘 is being stretched thin in any resource, money, staff or time; 入不敷出 says precisely that income is lower than spending.

cue: Every month the family's bills come to more than both salaries together, and their savings keep shrinking. How are their finances?

ctx.s: 他刚工作，工资不高，房租又贵，常常{入不敷出}。
ctx.en: He has just started working; his pay is low and his rent is high, so he often spends more than he earns.

ctx.s: 这家小餐馆开了一年，一直{入不敷出}，只好关门了。
ctx.en: The little restaurant ran at a loss for its whole first year and had to close.

ctx.s: “你每个月都{入不敷出}，还买这么贵的包？”
ctx.en: "You spend more than you earn every month, and you're still buying such an expensive bag?"

ctx.s: 老人看病花了很多钱，家里渐渐{入不敷出}了。
ctx.en: The old man's medical bills were large, and gradually the family's spending outran its income.

ctx.s: 由于游客减少，这个景区已经连续几年{入不敷出}。
ctx.en: Because visitor numbers fell, the scenic area has run a deficit for several years in a row.

ctx.s: 如果不控制开支，学校的经费很快就会{入不敷出}。
ctx.en: If spending is not controlled, the school's budget will soon fall short of its costs.

bad.s: 这次考试我{入不敷出}，分数比上次低。
bad.en: (meant: I did worse in this exam than last time)
bad.why: It is only about money coming in and going out, not about results or performance.

bad.s: 他是个{入不敷出}的人，从来不请客。
bad.en: (meant: he is stingy and never treats anyone)
bad.why: It describes a financial situation, not a stingy character; a stingy person is xiǎoqi.

lit: to pour out the household and sweep away the property

use.how: Predicate, or result after 弄得/落得/让: 赌博让他倾家荡产。 Said of a person or family ruined by gambling, bad investment, illness or disaster.

near.diff: 一贫如洗 describes the state of being utterly penniless; 倾家荡产 is the event of losing everything one used to own.

cue: In one year a shopkeeper gambles away his savings, his house and finally the shop itself. What has happened to him?

ctx.s: 他沉迷赌博，最后{倾家荡产}。
ctx.en: He became addicted to gambling and in the end lost everything he owned.

ctx.s: “炒股要小心，别弄得{倾家荡产}。”
ctx.en: "Be careful trading stocks; don't end up losing everything."

ctx.s: 为了给儿子治病，这对夫妻几乎{倾家荡产}。
ctx.en: To pay for their son's treatment, the couple spent almost everything they had.

ctx.s: 一场大火烧光了仓库，老板一夜之间{倾家荡产}。
ctx.en: A fire burned down the warehouse, and the owner was ruined overnight.

ctx.s: 有人借高利贷去投资，结果落得{倾家荡产}的下场。
ctx.en: Some people borrow from loan sharks to invest and end up completely ruined.

ctx.s: 就算{倾家荡产}，我也要把这场官司打下去。
ctx.en: Even if it costs me everything I have, I will fight this lawsuit to the end.

bad.s: 他做生意很成功，{倾家荡产}地赚了很多钱。
bad.en: (meant: his business succeeded and he made a fortune)
bad.why: It means losing one's whole fortune, the opposite of making one.

bad.s: 赌博{倾家荡产}了他的父亲。
bad.en: (meant: gambling ruined his father)
bad.why: It takes no object; make the ruined person the subject, with ràng: gambling made his father lose everything.

mean: genuine goods at a fair price; real and true
lit: the goods are genuine and the price is honest

use.how: Predicate or attributive with 的: 这家店货真价实；货真价实的专家。 First about goods, then about anything that is truly what it claims to be.

near.diff: 名副其实 says a name or reputation matches reality; 货真价实 is more colloquial, starts from goods, and stresses 'real, not fake'.

cue: At a market stall the honey is pure and fairly priced, unlike the fake stuff sold at tourist shops. How does a shopper praise the stall?

ctx.s: 这家小店的东西{货真价实}，回头客特别多。
ctx.en: This little shop sells genuine goods at fair prices, so it has lots of regular customers.

ctx.s: “放心买吧，我们卖的都是{货真价实}的新疆大枣。”
ctx.en: "Buy with confidence; all our dates are the real thing from Xinjiang."

ctx.s: 网上买东西，怎么知道是不是{货真价实}呢？
ctx.en: When you shop online, how can you tell whether the goods are genuine?

ctx.s: 他可不是冒牌的，是{货真价实}的医生。
ctx.en: He's no fake; he is a real, qualified doctor.

ctx.s: 这部电影没有花哨的宣传，却是一部{货真价实}的好作品。
ctx.en: The film had no flashy publicity, but it is a genuinely good piece of work.

ctx.s: 这家老字号开了一百多年，靠的就是{货真价实}。
ctx.en: This old brand has been open for over a century, and it owes that to honest goods at honest prices.

bad.s: 他对朋友{货真价实}，从来不说谎。
bad.en: (meant: he is sincere with his friends and never lies)
bad.why: It says a thing or person is genuinely what it claims to be, not that someone treats others honestly; use zhēnchéng (sincere).

bad.s: 我们要{货真价实}每一位顾客。
bad.en: (meant: we must treat every customer honestly)
bad.why: It is not a verb and cannot take an object; for treating customers honestly, use chéngshí (honest).

mean: to keep at something steadily over time
lit: to hold on to it with constancy

use.how: Predicate or adverbial (持之以恒地), often in advice: 学语言要持之以恒。 About keeping up a regular effort or habit over a long period.

near.diff: 坚持不懈 stresses not slackening in the face of difficulty; 持之以恒 stresses steady, regular effort kept up over a long time.

cue: A coach tells a beginner that twenty minutes of running every day for a year beats one exhausting week of training. What quality is the coach asking for?

ctx.s: 学外语没有捷径，每天学一点，关键是{持之以恒}。
ctx.en: There is no shortcut to learning a foreign language: study a little every day, and the key is to keep it up steadily.

ctx.s: “减肥不能三天两头换方法，少吃多动，{持之以恒}才有效。”
ctx.en: "You can't switch diets every few days; eat less, move more and keep it up steadily, that's what works."

ctx.s: 他每天早上跑步，十年来{持之以恒}，身体一直很好。
ctx.en: He has run every morning without fail for ten years, and he has always been healthy.

ctx.s: 只要每天练一会儿，{持之以恒}，你的钢琴一定会越弹越好。
ctx.en: As long as you practise a little every day and keep it up, your piano playing will keep getting better.

ctx.s: 很多人新年都会定计划，可是能一年到头{持之以恒}的有几个？
ctx.en: Lots of people make New Year plans, but how many keep them up steadily all year round?

ctx.s: 老师在评语里写道：希望你在学习上{持之以恒}，不要三天打鱼两天晒网。
ctx.en: The teacher wrote in the report: I hope you keep up your studies steadily instead of working in fits and starts.

bad.s: 他{持之以恒}了三天，就放弃了。
bad.en: (meant: he kept at it for three days, then gave up)
bad.why: It praises perseverance over a long period; it cannot describe a three-day effort that ends in giving up.

bad.s: 他是一个很{持之以恒}的人，脾气从来不变。
bad.en: (meant: he is a steady person whose temper never changes)
bad.why: It means persevering in an effort, not having a stable personality or mood.

mean: careful and conscientious in one's duties
lit: cautious and fearful, as if in constant danger

story.text: The phrase is very old. In the Book of Songs, in the ode 'Yun Han', a king facing a terrible drought describes himself with these words, trembling with dread 'as if before thunder'. Originally it meant anxious, fearful caution; over time it came to mean the careful, conscientious way a responsible person does their job.

use.how: Predicate, attributive or adverbial (兢兢业业地工作). Praises someone's long, careful and dutiful work, often an ordinary worker's.

near.diff: 勤勤恳恳 stresses diligence and hard work; 兢兢业业 adds carefulness and a strong sense of responsibility, of not wanting to make mistakes.

cue: At a retirement party, colleagues praise a clerk who for thirty years never let a careless error into the accounts. How do they describe her work?

ctx.s: 他几十年如一日，在岗位上{兢兢业业}，从来没出过差错。
ctx.en: For decades, day in and day out, he has done his job conscientiously and never made a mistake.

ctx.s: 王老师在这所学校{兢兢业业}地工作了三十年。
ctx.en: Mr Wang worked conscientiously at this school for thirty years.

ctx.s: “我爸当了一辈子会计，{兢兢业业}，没拿过别人一分钱。”
ctx.en: "My dad was an accountant all his life, careful and dutiful, and never took a cent that wasn't his."

ctx.s: 像她这样{兢兢业业}的人，为什么一直没有升职？
ctx.en: Why has someone as conscientious as her never been promoted?

ctx.s: 正是这些默默无闻、{兢兢业业}的普通员工，撑起了整个公司。
ctx.en: It is these unnoticed, dutiful ordinary employees who hold the whole company up.

ctx.s: 退休那天，老站长说：我只是{兢兢业业}做好了自己的本职工作。
ctx.en: On the day he retired, the old stationmaster said: I simply did my own job carefully and conscientiously.

bad.s: 他玩新游戏{兢兢业业}，一玩就是一整天。
bad.en: (meant: he is very devoted to his new game and plays all day)
bad.why: It praises the careful performance of work or duties, not enthusiasm for a hobby.

bad.s: 他害怕考试，紧张得{兢兢业业}的。
bad.en: (meant: he was so nervous about the exam he was trembling)
bad.why: Although it once meant 'fearful', today it only means conscientious in one's duties, never nervousness.

mean: with skill to spare, handling it effortlessly
lit: the blade moves freely with room to spare

story.text: Cook Ding carved an ox for Lord Wenhui so smoothly that it looked like a dance. He explained that he did not hack at bone but followed the natural gaps between the joints: the gaps have space, and the edge of his knife has no thickness, so the blade moves through them with room to spare. An ordinary cook changes his knife every month; his had lasted nineteen years and was still as sharp as new.

use.how: Predicate, often after 得 or 在……中: 处理得游刃有余。 Credits a person's skill and experience in a demanding job or situation.

near.diff: 得心应手 says one's hands do just what the mind wants; 游刃有余 stresses spare capacity, coping easily even with something complex.
轻而易举 says the task itself is easy; 游刃有余 says a hard task is easy for this skilled person.

cue: A veteran interpreter handles a tense three-way negotiation, switching languages calmly and even smoothing over an awkward joke. How was her performance?

ctx.s: 他用中文做报告，还能随口开几句玩笑，真是{游刃有余}。
ctx.en: He gives the presentation in Chinese and even throws in a few off-the-cuff jokes; he handles it with room to spare.

ctx.s: 面对记者的刁钻问题，发言人回答得{游刃有余}。
ctx.en: Faced with the reporters' tricky questions, the spokesperson answered with complete ease.

ctx.s: “你一个人管三个部门，忙得过来吗？”“放心，我应付得{游刃有余}。”
ctx.en: "You're running three departments by yourself; can you cope?" "Don't worry, I'm handling it with room to spare."

ctx.s: 刚当老师时他手忙脚乱，现在同时管两个班也{游刃有余}了。
ctx.en: When he first started teaching he was all at sea; now he runs two classes at once with ease.

ctx.s: 经过多年的历练，她在复杂的人际关系中也能{游刃有余}。
ctx.en: After years of experience, she moves through even complicated relationships with ease.

ctx.s: 这位老厨师掌勺几十年，一个人做一桌宴席都{游刃有余}。
ctx.en: This old chef has cooked for decades; he can prepare a whole banquet alone without breaking a sweat.

bad.s: 这个箱子很轻，我{游刃有余}地搬起来了。
bad.en: (meant: the box was light and I lifted it easily)
bad.why: It credits skill in complex work or situations, not physical ease with a trivial task; use qīng ér yì jǔ or simply qīngsōng.

bad.s: 他很快就{游刃有余}了这个难题。
bad.en: (meant: he quickly handled this difficult problem with ease)
bad.why: It describes how someone copes and cannot take an object; say chǔlǐ de yóu rèn yǒu yú (handled it with ease).

mean: outstanding, head and shoulders above others
lit: to rise out of one's kind and stand above the crowd

story.text: In Mencius, the disciple Gongsun Chou asks how Confucius compared with others. Mencius quotes You Ruo: the qilin among beasts, the phoenix among birds, Mount Tai among hills and the sage among people all belong to their kind, yet they rise out of their kind and stand above the crowd; and since people first lived, none has been greater than Confucius.

use.how: Predicate or attributive: 他在同学中出类拔萃；出类拔萃的人才。 Describes a lasting quality of excellence compared with one's peers.

near.diff: 脱颖而出 is the moment of emerging ahead in a competition or selection; 出类拔萃 describes a lasting state of being far better than one's peers.

cue: A professor writes a reference for a student who has been far ahead of every classmate, year after year. How does she describe him?

ctx.s: 她从小学习就好，在同学中一直{出类拔萃}。
ctx.en: She has done well at school since she was little and has always stood far above her classmates.

ctx.s: “你们班谁最优秀？”“小李吧，各方面都{出类拔萃}。”
ctx.en: "Who's the best in your class?" "Xiao Li, I'd say; he's outstanding in every way."

ctx.s: 学校希望培养出更多{出类拔萃}的人才。
ctx.en: The school hopes to produce more outstanding talent.

ctx.s: 这家公司的产品设计在整个行业里都算得上{出类拔萃}。
ctx.en: This company's product design counts as outstanding in the whole industry.

ctx.s: 他的球技虽然{出类拔萃}，脾气却很差，教练很头疼。
ctx.en: His football skills are outstanding, but his temper is terrible and the coach is at his wits' end.

ctx.s: 推荐信写道：该生成绩{出类拔萃}，具有很强的研究能力。
ctx.en: The reference letter read: this student's results are outstanding and his research ability is strong.

bad.s: 他在比赛最后一轮{出类拔萃}，拿了冠军。
bad.en: (meant: in the final round he came out on top and won)
bad.why: It describes a lasting superiority, not the moment of coming out on top in one contest; that is tuō yǐng ér chū.

bad.s: 这家饭店的菜{出类拔萃}地好吃。
bad.en: (meant: this restaurant's food is exceptionally tasty)
bad.why: It is not an intensifying adverb before an adjective; say tèbié hǎochī, or make the restaurant itself the subject of the idiom.

mean: to stand out from the crowd
lit: the point of an awl pokes out through the bag

story.text: When Qin besieged Handan, Lord Pingyuan of Zhao needed twenty retainers to go with him to Chu but could find only nineteen. Mao Sui offered himself. The lord said a capable man is like an awl in a bag, whose point shows at once, yet in three years no one had noticed Mao Sui. Mao Sui replied that he was asking to be put in the bag today; had he been put in earlier, the whole awl would have come out, not just its tip.

use.how: Predicate, usually 从/在……中脱颖而出. About a person or product emerging ahead of many rivals in a competition, selection or market.

near.diff: 出类拔萃 describes lasting excellence over one's peers; 脱颖而出 is the act of breaking out ahead of many competitors and getting noticed.

cue: Five hundred people apply for a single design job; an unknown graduate's portfolio catches every judge's eye and she gets it. What did she do?

ctx.s: 她从几百名选手中{脱颖而出}，进入了决赛。
ctx.en: She beat hundreds of contestants to stand out and reach the final.

ctx.s: “面试的人那么多，你是怎么{脱颖而出}的？”
ctx.en: "With so many people interviewing, how did you manage to stand out?"

ctx.s: 这款小众手机凭借超长的续航在市场上{脱颖而出}。
ctx.en: This niche phone stood out in the market thanks to its very long battery life.

ctx.s: 那年的作文比赛里，一个农村孩子的文章意外{脱颖而出}。
ctx.en: In that year's essay competition, a village child's essay unexpectedly came out on top.

ctx.s: 新人演员在这部剧里{脱颖而出}，一下子成了热门人物。
ctx.en: The newcomer stood out in the series and became famous almost overnight.

ctx.s: 想要在激烈的竞争中{脱颖而出}，光靠运气是不够的。
ctx.en: If you want to stand out in fierce competition, luck alone is not enough.

bad.s: 他{脱颖而出}了教室，去操场踢球。
bad.en: (meant: he rushed out of the classroom to play football)
bad.why: Its 'coming out' is not physically leaving a place; it means emerging ahead of rivals, and it takes no place object.

bad.s: 他一直{脱颖而出}，十年来都是班里第一。
bad.en: (meant: he has always been outstanding, top of the class for ten years)
bad.why: It is the moment of emerging from a crowd of rivals, not a lasting state; for that use chū lèi bá cuì.

mean: deliberately unconventional, trying to be different
lit: to put up the new and set up the different

story.text: A New Account of Tales of the World records that the monk Zhi Dun, discussing Zhuangzi's chapter 'Free and Easy Wandering', put forward new ideas beyond the two famous commentaries and different views from all the scholars, insights none of them had reached. In this origin the phrase was praise; today it more often hints that someone is being different just to be different.

use.how: Predicate, or after 为了/故意/一味: 不能只为了标新立异。 About ideas, dress or designs that break with convention, usually implying it is for show.

near.diff: 别出心裁 praises an original, inventive idea; 标新立异 usually suggests being different for its own sake, to attract attention.

cue: A student dyes his hair green and writes his essay in a strange made-up format, not because it helps, but just so he is like no one else. What is he doing?

ctx.s: 他穿得这么奇怪，就是想{标新立异}，吸引别人注意。
ctx.en: He dresses so oddly just to be different and get people's attention.

ctx.s: 设计要考虑实用，不能只为了{标新立异}。
ctx.en: A design has to be practical; it can't just be about being unconventional.

ctx.s: “你这个方案是认真的，还是故意{标新立异}？”
ctx.en: "Is this plan of yours serious, or are you just being different on purpose?"

ctx.s: 有些餐厅一味{标新立异}，菜做得好看却不好吃。
ctx.en: Some restaurants are so bent on being unusual that their dishes look good but taste bad.

ctx.s: 年轻人喜欢{标新立异}，这本身不是坏事，关键要有真本事。
ctx.en: Young people like to be different, which isn't bad in itself; what matters is having real ability.

ctx.s: 评论家认为，这位导演的新片{标新立异}有余，内涵不足。
ctx.en: Critics felt the director's new film had plenty of novelty for its own sake but little substance.

bad.s: 他上个月{标新立异}地搬进了新家。
bad.en: (meant: last month he moved into a new home)
bad.why: The 'new' in it means new ideas or styles; the idiom has nothing to do with new things like a house.

bad.s: 这个城市每年都{标新立异}，变化很大。
bad.en: (meant: the city renews itself every year and changes a lot)
bad.why: It describes someone deliberately pursuing unconventional ideas or style, not a place changing fast; for that say rì xīn yuè yì.
